questions.question: What does blocking cargo do?

options.text: Puts the cargo in a large box
Stops cargo from sliding during transport
Prevents others from buying the cargo

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops cargo from sliding during transport
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing prevent cargo from shifting while the vehicle is moving.

questions.question: Which of the following is a good rule when turning?

options.text: Use your arms to get other drivers' attention.
Turn off your turn signal before entering the turn.

questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn so drivers behind you know what you plan to do. Keep your signal on during the turn and turn it off when the turn is complete.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment:

options.text: The parking brake should not be set.
The gearshift should be in first gear.

questions.explanation: Before you check the engine compartment, set the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine compartment before you get in the cab or start the engine.

questions.question: If you test positive for any alcohol, even below the legal limit, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If any alcohol is found in your system, but you are still below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A stopped bus:

options.text: Is not a concern since it is stopped.
Is only a concern if passengers are leaving the bus.
Is a concern whether or not you see passengers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern whether or not you see passengers.
questions.explanation: Always be careful when driving near a stopped bus. Passengers may be nearby. The bus may block their view of you or your view of them.

questions.question: Always do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order because:

options.text: You will be less likely to forget a step.
You will finish the inspection faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Using the same order for every inspection helps you learn the steps. Following a set checklist means you are less likely to skip something.

questions.question: Broken suspension parts:

options.text: Should be fixed, but not right away.

questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle, supports its load, and keeps the axles in place. When inspecting your vehicle, check for damaged or missing spring hangers, spring leaves, shock absorbers, u-bolts, and frame members. Broken suspension parts are very dangerous.

questions.question: When you start your vehicle, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Jump quickly from low to high.

questions.explanation: Check your gauges before starting your trip. After you start the engine, the coolant temperature should rise slowly to the normal operating temperature.

questions.question: States verify that a CDL or CLP driver has only one license by:

options.text: Using a computer system that connects all states.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using a computer system that connects all states.
questions.explanation: All U.S. states share CDL and CLP license information in a computer database. When you apply for a license in one state, that state checks the database to make sure you do not already have one in another state.

questions.question: When using a fire extinguisher on a fire, you should:

options.text: Get as close to the fire as possible.
Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
Aim at the top of the flames.
Aim at the ground about two feet away from the fire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay as far away from the fire as possible.
questions.explanation: When using a fire extinguisher, stay as far from the flames as possible and aim at the base of the fire.

questions.question: During the on-road driving test, you will be graded on how you use your lane. Which of these is poor lane usage?

options.text: Not driving over curbs or sidewalks
Driving in the left lane when more than one lane is available
Finishing a right turn in the right lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving in the left lane when more than one lane is available
questions.explanation: During the on-road driving test, do not drive over curbs, sidewalks, or lane markings. Stop behind stop lines, crosswalks, or stop signs. On roads with multiple lanes, complete turns in the correct lane. Always use or stay in the right lane unless it is blocked.

questions.question: In a basic vehicle control test, a look happens when:

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the instrument panel.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of their vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look happens when a driver opens the door, leaves their seat, and walks to the back of the vehicle to check its position. During the straight-line backing exercise, a driver can only take one look. During any other exercise, a driver can take up to two looks.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Only happens when a driver physically does something while driving.
Can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can happen from mental activities, like daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for an object), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like texting on a phone). To avoid distracted driving: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead of time, avoid serious conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before you leave, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:

options.text: Can damage parts of your vehicle.
Is needed to warm up vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can damage parts of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly so your vehicle does not jerk. Rough acceleration can cause damage to the engine and other parts.

questions.question: Before a trip, you check under your vehicle and see fresh oil. This is:
questions.explanation: Before starting a trip, check under your vehicle for fresh oil, coolant, grease, or fuel leaks. Finding any of these is a sign of a problem.

questions.question: When starting a trip with a load, the driver should:

options.text: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
Drive faster than normal to test if the load is secure.
Only use side mirrors to watch the cargo.
Not check the cargo again if it was secure before starting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and check the cargo within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check that cargo is secure before you start. Check it again within the first 50 miles. After that, check it every three hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Remove water and oil from the air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tank.
questions.explanation: Air storage tanks need to be drained to remove water and oil that build up. If you do not drain them, the tank can be damaged. Open the drains at the end of each day of driving.

questions.question: Mirrors should be adjusted:

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start your trip. If your vehicle has a trailer, you can only check mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: May need to steer around it.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to steer around it.
questions.explanation: Stopping is not always the best way to avoid a hazard. If you do not have enough space to stop, steering around it may be safer.

questions.question: When should you turn off a turn signal?
questions.explanation: If your vehicle does not have self-canceling turn signals, turn off the signal after you finish turning.

questions.question: A commercial driver with a blood alcohol level (BAC) below 0.04 percent will be:

options.text: Taken out of service for 24 hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: Taken out of service for 24 hours.
questions.explanation: If you operate a commercial vehicle with any detectable alcohol in your system, even below 0.04 percent, you will be taken out of service for 24 hours. Driving while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: Headache racks:
questions.explanation: Headache racks are protective barriers at the front of a truck. They protect the driver from cargo that may shift during a crash or emergency stop.

questions.question: The parking brake should be:

options.text: Used to stop during normal driving.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you, you should:
questions.explanation: If someone is tailgating you, create space ahead of your vehicle so they can pass. Do not speed up. The other driver may just tailgate you at the higher speed, making it more dangerous.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.explanation: You need good traction to brake and steer your vehicle safely. Make sure your tires are in good condition before you drive.

questions.question: A tank endorsement is required to:
questions.explanation: A tank endorsement is required to operate a tank vehicle carrying either liquids or gases.

questions.question: Mirrors should be:

options.text: Checked only if you suspect a problem.

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This helps you stay aware of traffic and monitor your vehicle for any problems.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should be:
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must be properly secured and in good condition. They should not be loose, broken, missing, or rubbing against other parts of the vehicle.

questions.question: What is the Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR)?

options.text: The maximum total weight allowed for a vehicle and its cargo.
The minimum weight allowed for a trailer.
The maximum weight allowed for a trailer and its cargo.
The maximum weight allowed for a tractor only.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum total weight allowed for a vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: The GVWR is the maximum combined weight of a vehicle and its load set by the manufacturer.

questions.question: Retreaded tires:

options.text: Can be used anywhere on a bus.
Can be used on the front of a bus.
Can be used on the rear of a bus.
Cannot be used on a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be used on the rear of a bus.
questions.explanation: Retreaded tires cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus. They can only be used on the rear wheels.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, first drive past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the parking space. The vehicle must be parked straight and within the parking space lines.

questions.question: Rough acceleration:
questions.explanation: Always speed up slowly and smoothly. Jerky acceleration can damage your vehicle's engine.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, your brakes may fade. What does brake fade mean?

options.text: They work unevenly between front and back.

questions.explanation: Using your brakes too much on a steep downhill can cause them to overheat and work poorly. To prevent brake overheating on hills, use engine braking instead.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a reason to shift to a higher gear?
questions.explanation: There are two reasons to shift to a higher gear: engine speed (RPMs) and road speed (mph). Check your vehicle's manual for the correct RPM range. Watch your speedometer and shift up when needed based on speed. Time is not a factor in deciding when to shift gears.

questions.question: How long is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: The average driver's reaction time is three-quarters to one second.

questions.question: A commercial truck driver:

options.text: Can use any cell phone while driving.
Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
Can only use a cell phone on rural roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can only use a hands-free cell phone while driving, if allowed.
questions.explanation: If you use a cell phone while driving a commercial vehicle, use only a hands-free phone placed within easy reach. Even hands-free phones can distract you from driving. Know the cell phone laws in the state where you are driving.

questions.question: Distracted driving:

options.text: Is caused only by physical distractions.
Gets worse if you pre-program radio stations.
Can be reduced by avoiding conversation with others.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be reduced by avoiding conversation with others.
questions.explanation: Distractions can be physical (like reaching for something), mental (like talking with a passenger), or both (like texting). To avoid distraction: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, avoid serious or emotional conversations while driving, adjust mirrors before leaving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, should you speed up to shake them off?
questions.explanation: Do not speed up when being tailgated. The other driver will likely just follow you at the higher speed, making it even more dangerous.

questions.question: When alley docking, how should your vehicle be parked?

options.text: With the front bumper on the front boundary line.
With the rear wheels over the rear boundary line.
Straight within the parking space lines.
At an angle within the parking space lines.

questions.correctAnswerText: Straight within the parking space lines.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, first drive past the alley and stop parallel to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the parking space. The vehicle must be parked straight and within the parking space lines.

questions.question: Before a pre-trip inspection, why should you look under the vehicle?

options.text: To see if the vehicle is on an incline.
To check for fresh fluid leaks.
To see if it is parked in a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: To check for fresh fluid leaks.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting your vehicle, check its overall condition. Look under it for fresh leaks of oil, grease, or fuel. Also check around the vehicle for hazards like other vehicles, people, or low-hanging wires or branches.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Leave the keys in the ignition.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal level when you start a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: If you pull over on the side of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Use the taillights to alert other motorists.
Keep your lights off to avoid distracting other drivers.
Set out items from the cab to warn motorists.

questions.explanation: If you stop on the side of the road, turn on your emergency flashers and place warning signals to alert other drivers.

questions.question: What should you do before driving down a hill?
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before going downhill. Drive at a speed where you do not need to use your brakes too much.

questions.question: A visual low pressure warning signal should activate before air pressure drops between ____ psi.
questions.explanation: A visual low pressure warning signal activates before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi. This signal can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a result of drinking alcohol and driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows reaction time and causes poor driving. Alcohol can cause drivers to straddle lanes, make jerky starts, forget to signal, run stop signs and red lights, and pass unsafely. Alcohol always slows your ability to react.

questions.question: When changing lanes, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals.

questions.explanation: Always use your turn signals and check your mirrors when changing lanes.

questions.question: What can a trailer brake hand valve be used for?

options.text: Stop the vehicle from rolling back when starting from a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the vehicle from rolling back when starting from a stop.
questions.explanation: If equipped, the trailer brake hand valve stops the vehicle from rolling back when you start from a stop.

questions.question: What should be true about the leaves on a leaf spring?
questions.explanation: Check that leaf springs have no missing or broken leaves. If one-fourth or more of the leaves are missing, the vehicle must be taken out of service until it is fixed.

questions.question: What is the minimum tread depth for tires that are NOT on the front of a truck?
questions.explanation: Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread depth in every major groove. Other tires must have at least 2/32 inch of tread depth. All tires on the vehicle should be the same size.
